item.content:encoded:
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman is recovering quickly after a scary injury.
Bregman suffered multiple facial fractures after a foul ball off the bat of first baseman Michael Busch hit him while he was standing in the on-deck circle during Chicago's 9-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Sunday. Luckily for the Cubs, the injury won't require surgery. Even better for Chicago, he could return to the lineup soon.
Counsell spoke with the media Tuesday before the Cubs faced the Miami Marlins in the first of their three-game homestand. The skipper said Bregman is in a "good place" and they're not placing him on the injured list. Counsell added Bregman may return for the final week of the regular season. (Entering Tuesday, the National League Central squad had six games remaining.)
Cubs president Jed Hoyer, meanwhile, exercised more caution when discussing Bregman's status. The executive said he wants to see how the third baseman responds to increased activity before reinserting him into the lineup. Taking a close look at Bregman's face explains why Hoyer remains ultracareful.
Craig Counsell announced that Alex Bregman will not be placed on the injured list. pic.twitter.com/3aoA8f6RWs
— Marquee Sports Network (@WatchMarquee) September 22, 2026
Jed Hoyer Addresses the Alex Bregman Injury and Next Steps pic.twitter.com/nA3GDTeukj
— CHGO Cubs (@CHGO_Cubs) September 22, 2026
Bregman arrived at Wrigley Field before the Cubs played the Marlins. His left eye was still bruised and his face swollen, but he's in better shape than he was on Sunday. Shortly after suffering the injury, the infielder shared a selfie on his Instagram story. His eye was swollen shut and his face bloodied.
Expect Bregman to put plenty of ice packs on his face over the next few days as he aims to return promptly. When he does, the three-time All-Star could be an instant difference-maker for a Cubs team hoping to make noise in the postseason. Chicago (87-69) can no longer win the division after the Milwaukee Brewers (98-58) clinched it, but it could secure one of three NL wild-card seeds. The team is in a chaotic race with the San Diego Padres (87-69), Philadelphia Phillies (86-70) and Arizona Diamondbacks (82-74). (All records were entering Tuesday.)
Assuming the Cubs grab one of those spots, Bregman, a proven postseason performer, should then deliver in October. The two-time World Series champion slashed .239/.349/.442 on 380 postseason at-bats in his first eight seasons with the Houston Astros and Boston Red Sox.
Bregman could produce more postseason magic after slashing .262/.352/.452 on his first 600 at-bats for the Cubs this season. If he does, Chicago will be even more thrilled that his injury was less severe than initially anticipated.

CHICAGO (AP) — Griffin Conine drove in Esteury Ruiz with a tiebreaking single in Miami's six-run 12th inning, and the Marlins stymied Chicago's push for an NL wild card with an 8-2 victory over the Cubs on Tuesday night.
Conine put Miami ahead to stay with his well-placed blooper to left field. Jakob Marsee added a run-scoring single, and Joe Mack capped the outburst with a two-run single.
Kyle Stowers hit a solo homer for the Marlins (77-80), who had lost three in a row. Josh Ekness (3-4) pitched a scoreless inning for the win.
The Cubs (87-70) could have clinched a playoff berth with a win or an Arizona loss, but the Diamondbacks won 7-2 at Colorado.
Chicago, San Diego and Philadelphia are tied atop the wild-card standings for all three NL spots. The Phillies posted a 6-4 victory over Milwaukee on Tuesday night, and the Padres lost 7-0 to the Los Angeles Dodgers.
The Cubs had a chance to win the game in the 10th, loading the bases with two down. But Miami second baseman Javier Sanoja robbed Pedro Ramírez of a game-ending single with a terrific sliding stop.
Caleb Thielbar (3-4) was charged with the loss.
Chicago played without third baseman Alex Bregman, who is recovering from multiple facial fractures after he was struck in the face by a foul ball. The three-time All-Star could return to the lineup before the end of the regular season this weekend.
Miami jumped in front when Stowers doubled and scored on Agustín Ramírez's single in the fourth. Stowers added his 20th homer in the sixth.
Chicago rallied in the bottom half, putting runners on the corners with no outs. Michael Busch then hit a hard grounder to first, but Mack mishandled Deyvison De Los Santos' throw to the plate and Pete Crow-Armstrong scampered home with the Cubs' first run. One batter later, Ian Happ hit a tying single off Calvin Faucher.

Ryan Gusto (1-5, 4.14 ERA) starts for Miami on Wednesday night, and fellow right-hander Kevin Gausman (9-12, 4.55) pitches for Chicago.

item.content:encoded:
CHICAGO -- If Alex Bregman is not spotted in the Cubs’ locker room before a game, chances are he is down the tunnel in the batting cage. That was no different on Tuesday afternoon, even with his left cheek and eye still bruised and swollen from the foul ball that struck him in the on-deck circle on Sunday in Cincinnati.
“He’s completely himself,” Cubs manager Craig Counsell said. “He can’t sit still. He’s all over the room. Those are really good signs.”
All the worst-case scenarios that immediately came to mind for anyone who witnessed Sunday’s freak accident have, by all accounts, been avoided. Bregman has had multiple appointments with a variety of specialists and has received positive news on all fronts. His vision is fine. There are multiple fractures in his cheek area, but no surgery is required.
Counsell noted prior to Tuesday’s game against the Marlins that Bregman would not be placed on the injured list and a return before the end of the regular season has not been ruled out. In the coming days, Bregman will continue to ramp up his activity to gauge whether any symptoms arise, and the Cubs’ medical and training staff will assess and proceed from there.
“I think Alex is going to be fine, I really do,” Counsell said. “He’s planning on playing. He knew he had to get some good news from the doctors. He got that good news. So he’s going to do everything in his power. And as long as symptoms don’t increase, or happen as he increases activity, I think you’re going to see him play.”
After this three-game series at home against the Marlins, the Cubs are scheduled to play three games against the Red Sox in Boston, where Bregman played last season. The North Siders headed into Tuesday atop the National League Wild Card standings.
In the fourth inning of Sunday’s 9-1 win over the Reds, Michael Busch checked his swing and fouled off a pitch from Cincinnati’s Luis Mey. The baseball hit the dirt and then struck Bregman in the face as he prepared to hit. The third baseman immediately dropped his bat, grabbed his face and headed down the dugout steps with members of Chicago’s staff.
Bregman was examined at a local hospital and cleared of any concussion symptoms. He posted photos on his Instagram account that showed severe swelling around his eye, but declared, “I’ll be back.” The Cubs had a staffer remain in Cincinnati to drive back to Chicago with Bregman, as opposed to having him fly back with the team.
“He doesn’t look great, that’s for sure,” Cubs president of baseball operations Jed Hoyer joked. “But no one loves to play more than him. I can say that with no equivocation. I’ve never had a player that loves baseball as much as he does. He just wants to play all the time. Right away, when we first heard from him afterwards, [he said] he was going to find a way to do it.
“There were scenarios where there was no way it was going to happen -- if he needed surgery or things like that. But he didn’t. Now he has the chance to get out there. And there’s nothing he wants to do more. It’s impressive.”
During the pregame hours on Tuesday, Bregman got a workout in and also donned a helmet and headed into the batting cage to track pitches on the high-velocity Trajekt machine. Around the clubhouse and in the cage, Bregman was very much acting like his usual self, which brought a smile to Nico Hoerner’s face.
“His reaction to everything has been uplifting,” Hoerner said. “Just in being relentlessly aggressive and positive and speaking about all the things he’s excited to do and turn it into. Just his own mentality kind of leads the group in that way in how to handle it. It was a super jarring thing and terrible timing, obviously.”
Through 153 games this season, the 32-year-old Bregman has hit .262 with 26 homers, 32 doubles, 89 RBIs and an .804 OPS. Since the All-Star break, however, only teammate Pete Crow-Armstrong (4.5) has been worth more wins above replacement (per FanGraphs) in the Majors than Bregman (3.4). The third baseman has hit .296 with 17 homers, 17 doubles, 48 RBIs and a .978 OPS in 59 games in the second half.
While Bregman is out, the Cubs have both Pedro Ramírez and Matt Shaw as options for third base. Ramírez -- recently the primary starter at second base, while Hoerner manned short with Dansby Swanson on the IL -- was in the lineup on Tuesday night. Shaw was Chicago’s main third baseman last year before Bregman came aboard via his five-year, $175 million deal.
“No one’s asking anyone to replace Breggy and what he’s done this year,” Hoerner said. “But in the meantime, we’re very well-equipped to handle it.”

item.content:encoded:
The Craig Breslow era in Boston has felt like a roller coaster ride. Hired at the start of the 2023-24 offseason, the Boston Red Sox have not had a losing season under Breslow, despite wild swings in the team's form over the three years.
With the Red Sox clinching a playoff berth for the second year in a row, team ownership decided that now was the time to exercise two options on their Chief Baseball Officer's contract, guaranteeing his deal for the 2029 and 2030 seasons. On the surface, a head of baseball operations who got his team to the playoffs in years two and three of their time running the club getting years added to their contract, would make sense, but in Breslow's case it isn't as straightforward.
It was only three months ago when most of Red Sox Nation was calling for Breslow's head. The Red Sox were 32-46 on June 24, dead last in the division, and it already seemed like the season was over. It took a miraculous turnaround to get the team to the playoffs. Not to say that Breslow had nothing to do with that; he had added a lot of players to the roster who were key contributors, but that has a lot more to do with the players and coaches than the front office.
Breslow's tenure has also been marred by controversy, specifically the Rafael Devers drama. It was his handling of the situation, along with former manager Alex Cora, that ultimately led to the fracture of the relationship with the team's then-face of the franchise. While the fanbase was split on whose side they took, player or team, his actions after the fact didn't make it any better.
Red Sox's Craig Breslow had the hottest seat of any GM only three months ago
It was the signing of Alex Bregman that caused the Devers drama in the first place. While Breslow was praised for the signing, Bregman opted out at the end of the year and was then not re-signed. The Red Sox went from two elite third basemen to none in the span of a season. It wasn't a good look for the Red Sox CBO.
Now, Breslow's pivot from all of the drama and mess surrounding Devers and Bregman looks incredibly good in hindsight. The additions of Ranger Suarez, Sonny Gray, Willson Contreras, Caleb Durbin, and others have been extremely impactful to the Red Sox's success this season. While some of those moves were celebrated at the time they happened, others like the Durbin-Kyle Harrison swap (that also netted the Red Sox Andruw Monasterio and Anthony Seigler) were heavily scrutinized.
Breslow also made good moves at the trade deadline, adding Erik Miller and Eli White, who have looked good for the Sox. He also made the splash trade for Adley Rutschman, which hasn't worked as well on the field, but certainly instilled confidence in the team, knowing the front office believed in them.
Red Sox could've softened the impact by extending one of Craig Breslow's options at first
All of this is to say that Breslow's time as CBO hasn't been as smooth sailing as the records would suggest. He has had some high highs but also some low lows. Why did ownership feel the need to exercise both options right now? The first option wasn't needed until the 2029 season, two years out. The second was for 2030, three years out.
Doing the first one now would've been fine — picking up the 2029 option gives Breslow another three comfortable seasons on his contract. That would make him more comfortable making moves for the future and give him the job security to know he will likely be in place to see them play out. Selecting the 2030 option on the same day was unnecessary, though.
There have been too many hiccups in the three years under Breslow to say he has warranted another four seasons. The start of 2026 could easily repeat itself in 2027. Should ownership feel the need to relieve him of his duties early, then this makes it that much harder. Breslow hasn't won a World Series in Boston; in fact, he hasn't even made it out of the Wild Card round. Exercising the option for 2030 feels very premature.
Breslow has not done a bad job in Boston. At the end of the day, it's results that matter, and Breslow's teams have made the playoffs two out of three times. He shouldn't be fearing for his job, but his contract also wasn't ending for another two seasons. It feels early to be handing him the keys so far down the road after the drama of his first two years as CBO.

El tercera base de los Cachorros de Chicago, Alex Bregman, sufrió múltiples fracturas faciales tras ser golpeado por un foul ball el domingo pasado, pero no requerirá cirugía y mantiene la esperanza de regresar a tiempo para los playoffs de las Grandes Ligas.
El incidente ocurrió en el cuarto inning del triunfo 9-1 de Chicago sobre los Rojos de Cincinnati. Michael Busch, bateador zurdo de los Cubs, cortó el swing ante un pitcheo de Luis Mey y la pelota rebotó en el terreno e impactó a Bregman, que se encontraba en el círculo de espera. El pelotero cubrió su rostro, salió del campo con sangrado y fue trasladado a un hospital para radiografías y tomografía.

Bregman presentó fracturas en el lado izquierdo del rostro, principalmente en el pómulo debajo del ojo. El ojo izquierdo quedó muy hinchado. El manager Craig Counsell describió el golpe como “un accidente terrible” y destacó que primero importaba el bienestar del jugador.
Bregman publicó en Instagram una foto de su rostro inflamado con el mensaje: “Thanks for all the messages yall. I’ll be back.” Al día siguiente, ya de regreso en Chicago, compartió otra imagen con la leyenda “Back in Chicago”.
Impacto para los Cubs rumbo a octubre
Bregman, de 32 años, firmó un contrato de cinco años y 175 millones de dólares con Chicago para 2026. Esta temporada registra .262 de average, 26 jonrones, 89 impulsadas y 5.2 WAR. En la segunda mitad ha estado especialmente caliente, con línea de .296/.378/.600.
Los Cubs están en la pelea por el primer wild card de la Liga Nacional, empatados o cerca de Padres y Filis con seis juegos por disputar. Se espera que Bregman vaya a la lista de lesionados de 10 días y se pierda el tramo final de la temporada regular en las series ante Marlins y Red Sox. Los playoffs comienzan el 29 de septiembre.
En su ausencia, Matt Shaw y el novato Pedro Ramírez podrían cubrir la tercera base. La visión del jugador se considera en buen estado, según fuentes cercanas al equipo. El propio Bregman, conocido por su intensidad, ha dejado claro que quiere volver lo antes posible. El club prioriza su recuperación y evaluará día a día si puede estar listo para la postemporada.

- MLB. Dave Roberts sobre Shohei Ohtani: “Hay una buena posibilidad de que lo veamos en la próxima serie”
En este momento, los Chicago Cubs necesitan que todos aporten al máximo para el tramo final de la temporada regular. El título de la división está fuera de alcance, pero el primer puesto en la carrera por el comodín de la Liga Nacional sigue en juego. Lamentablemente, el equipo perdió a uno de sus mejores jugadores para esta recta final el pasado fin de semana.
Alex Bregman sufrió una lesión terrible, y ocurrió de la manera más desafortunada posible. Mientras esperaba su turno en el círculo de espera (*on-deck circle*), Bregman recibió un golpe en la cara por una bola de foul bateada por un compañero de equipo. Sufrió múltiples fracturas faciales, y la imagen que se vio tras el incidente fue impactante.
La lesión de Bregman ha llevado a muchos aficionados a plantearse un par de cosas. En primer lugar, a muchos les sorprende que este tipo de incidentes no ocurran con más frecuencia. El margen de error es mínimo cuando los bateadores que esperan su turno se colocan tan cerca de la caja de bateo. Hemos visto situaciones similares antes, pero resulta algo sorprendente que no sean más habituales.
Trevor Plouffe pide a la MLB que proteja a los bateadores que esperan su turno en el futuro
Sin embargo, aunque no suceda tan a menudo como cabría suponer, incluso exjugadores de la MLB como Trevor Plouffe creen que ha llegado el momento de que el béisbol implemente cambios para evitar este tipo de lesiones en el futuro. Plouffe expresó su opinión el lunes en el podcast "Talkin’ Baseball".
"Hace falta que ocurra algo así. Por ejemplo, si esto hubiera pasado en los playoffs y, de repente, Alex Bregman ya no pudiera jugar, eso sacudiría a la gente y provocaría una reacción. Quizás esto ya sea lo suficientemente grave. ¿Qué tal si ponemos una red protectora o algo parecido?"
Simplemente no hay razón para que un jugador esté tan cerca cuando no está bateando activamente. Es cierto que estar tan cerca permite al bateador que espera su turno conocer mejor al lanzador que está en el montículo, pero eso también pueden hacerlo desde el dugout o contando con mayor protección a su alrededor.

item.content:encoded:
As we make our way through the final week of the regular season, there doesn't seem to be much suspense as to who will be named MVP. At least, that's what we can glean from our latest -- and final -- MLB.com 2026 MVP poll.
Yordan Alvarez is still well out in front in the American League despite relatively mediocre production of late. In the National League, Pete Crow-Armstrong is wrapping up one of the best all-around seasons in recent memory.
Thirty-eight MLB.com experts cast votes for who they think will earn MVP honors after this season, with 32 players receiving at least one vote. As a reminder, votes were based not only on results so far, but also on how things are expected to play out the rest of the season.
Voters ranked their top five picks in each league on a 5-4-3-2-1 scale -- five points for a first-place vote, four points for a second-place vote and so on. Here are the results.
All stats are through Sunday unless otherwise noted.
AMERICAN LEAGUE
Alvarez has been so good this year that what qualifies as a slump for him would be a good stretch for most other hitters. Over his past 41 games, he is hitting .264 with an .840 OPS. Again, not bad for most, but well below the standard of the AL leader in average (.313) and OPS (1.027). Alvarez has three homers and five RBIs through 16 games this month, leaving him tied with the O's Pete Alonso and one home run behind the Rays' Junior Caminero for the AL lead and nine RBIs behind Alonso for the top spot in that statistic. Even though his Triple Crown chances have faded, Alvarez has still put together an awesome 2026 at the plate. His 179 wRC+ is at least 27 points better than any other qualified hitter.
We know Caminero is one of the game's great sluggers. He is finishing up his second straight 40-homer season and swings harder than anyone. But what's been most impressive about his season is his improved strike-zone judgment. He has upped his walk rate from a below-average 6.3% to 11.5%, which ranks in the 80th percentile of MLB. He's also maintained a very solid strikeout rate (18.5%). He's not chasing as much, has shaved his whiff rate and is making more contact overall. That blend of patience, power and bat control is a special combination, especially in a 23-year-old player. Carrying a .363 on-base percentage (52 points better than last season), Caminero's .892 OPS ranks third in the AL.
Witt has had better offensive seasons, although 18 homers, 43 steals and a 119 wRC+ in 137 games is not too shabby. But when you consider his entire skill set, Witt remains extremely valuable. His +16 fielding run value is tied for third in the Majors, and his 22 outs above average tops the AL. He also has a +8 baserunning run value, one behind the D-backs' Corbin Carroll for the MLB lead. So while he hasn't been as undeniable in the batter's box as he was in 2024 (169 wRC+), Witt's all-around greatness has him atop the AL FanGraphs WAR leaderboard (6.6) and in line for a possible top-five finish in the MVP voting for the third time in three years.
There has been quite a bit of MVP chatter surrounding Schlittler in recent weeks. And why not? He is pacing the AL in ERA (1.94), WHIP (0.91) and FanGraphs pitching WAR (6.1). He ranks second in the junior circuit in opponents' batting average (.182) and strikeout-minus-walk rate (25.0%). He has allowed one or zero runs in 21 starts. That's a Yankees franchise record and something only two other pitchers age-25 or younger have accomplished in the Live Ball Era (since 1920): Blake Snell (2018) and Dean Chance (1964). He seems like a lock for the AL Cy Young Award at this point, but Schlittler will receive his fair share of MVP love.
Schlittler hasn't been the only indispensable Yankee this year. While New York has been without Aaron Judge for a large portion of the season and has missed other star bats as well due to injuries, Rice has been a constant. He ranks third in the AL in homers (39) and runs scored (100). He's fourth in the league in RBIs (95) and OPS (.888), and tied for fourth in batting run value (+34). With two homers during the final week, Rice would become just the second non-Judge Yankee over the past decade to hit at least 41 homers in a season, joining Juan Soto (2024).
Others receiving votes: Willson Contreras, Red Sox; Pete Alonso, Orioles; Kevin McGonigle, Tigers; Miguel Vargas, White Sox; Randy Arozarena, Mariners; Munetaka Murakami, White Sox; Dylan Cease, Blue Jays
NATIONAL LEAGUE
Last month, PCA jumped over Ohtani and into the No. 1 spot in our poll. This month, he has run away from the rest of the field. The recipient of every first-place vote cast by our panel, Crow-Armstrong is tied with Kyle Schwarber for the MLB lead in home runs (45). No one has more runs (118), extra-base hits (83) or total bases (351) this season. With 38 steals, the Cubs' dynamic center fielder could become the seventh member of the 40-40 club later this week. Oh, and let's not overlook the fact that he is arguably the best defensive player at any position right now. It's no longer a question of whether Crow-Armstrong is the NL MVP. The award is as good as his right now. But will he win it in unanimous fashion?
Ohtani remains the clear runner-up in the NL despite playing in just three games this month due to his nagging left knee and right biceps injuries. The good news is Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said "there's a good chance" Ohtani will be activated from the 15-day injured list Wednesday after a minimum stint. He won't pitch for the rest of the season, leaving him with a 1.79 ERA and 95 K's over 85 2/3 innings. But Ohtani will have a few games to add to his offensive totals (30 homers, 142 wRC+).
We mentioned earlier how Schlittler looks like the heavy favorite for the AL Cy Young Award. Misiorowski is an even bigger shoo-in in the senior circuit. Through 169 1/3 innings, Miz leads the Majors in just about every category, including ERA (1.86), WHIP (0.80), strikeout-minus-walk rate (31.7%) and fWAR (6.5), to name just a few. Opposing batters have a scant .474 OPS against Misiorowski, which is the second-lowest by any qualified starter in the Divisional Era (since 1969). Pedro Martinez, in one of the greatest seasons by a pitcher, recorded a .473 opponents' OPS in 2000.
De La Cruz, who didn't receive a single vote in our previous MVP poll, has been red-hot for Cincinnati over the past month. In his last 27 games, he is batting .404 with eight homers, six steals and a 1.205 OPS. He collected multiple hits in 14 of those games, and his 2.5 fWAR during this period is the best in the big leagues. This prolonged hot streak has given De La Cruz a career-best 139 wRC+ and has left him two homers and two steals away from becoming the fourth Red in the 30-30 club and the first since Brandon Phillips in 2007.
Schwarber has fallen into a bit of a rut, going 4-for-34 with one home run over his past 10 games. He's also eight strikeouts away from setting a new record for K's in a single season. Even so, you have to admire Schwarber's consistency. He will end up with more than 40 homers and 150 games played in four of the past five seasons. He has surpassed 100 walks for a fourth consecutive season, and a third NL home run title is right there for the taking, too.

So much so that it could come down to the final weekend of the regular season, when the Cubs are slated to square off against another playoff-bound team, the Boston Red Sox, at Fenway Park.
There's just one problem here.
The weather forecast looks awful for the Northeast, so much so that playing any baseball feels like a stretch if these forecase models come to life.
Crowded NL playoff picture could be complicated by awful Red Sox weather forecast
Entering Tuesday, the Cubs and Padres are tied for the first spot in the Wild Card standings, with the Philadelphia Phillies just one game back and the Arizona Diamondbacks clinging for deal life with playoff hopes hanging by a thread. It's completely feasible that, given how crowded things are in the NL Wild Card race, those games between the Cubs and Red Sox are critical in determining the pecking order.
I have no idea what happens if the entire weekend gets washed. The playoff schedule is set and, with the expanded field, balancing the national broadcast schedule across multiple networks is no easy feat. In other words, shifting the whole postseason back a day or two feels like a long-shot, at best.
Could we get a neutral site series for the final weekend? That would really be the cherry on top of a season that's been filled with oddities and strange luck for the Cubs. But, hey, as we all remember when 'neutral site games' come to mind, maybe we'll get a Carlos Zambrano v. the Astros at Miller Park-esque performance?
Probably not, so let's just stay tuned to see how the week takes shape.

item.content:encoded:
Shortly after the Boston Red Sox lost out on Alex Bregman in free agency, fans looked to find the reunion between the two sides. The Chicago Cubs will be in town for the final series of the season from September 25-27, but the reunion with Bregman will probably look much different than fans expected days ago.
On September 20, while he was standing near the on-deck circle warming up for his next at-bat, Bregman was hit in the face with a foul ball. The ball shot off Michael Busch's bat on a line and hit the third baseman square in the cheek. It happened so fast there was no chance of dodging it. He immediately buried his face in his hands and descended the dugout steps with a trainer.
After the game, Bregman shared a picture of his face (don't click if you're squeamish), featuring a swollen-shut black eye and a bloodied cheek. He posted another picture the following morning and the entire left half of his face was swollen.
The Cubs sent Bregman to the hospital after the injury. According to Chicago manager Craig Counsell said Bregman was hit in the left cheekbone just under his eye and his nose was bleeding after the hit. Jeff Passan on September 21 reported that Bregman has multiple facial fractures and that he will not undergo surgery — although that doesn't exactly mean he doesn't need it. Passan says Bregman hopes to return during the postseason, but he might be too banged up to pull it off.
Alex Bregman not likley to play in Cubs series against Red Sox following unlucky hit by foul ball near the on-deck circle
While there's still no diagnosis, it's hard to forsee Bregman returning from this injury in a timely manner. Not only will he most likely miss his series at Fenway Park, but he could be out for Chicago's playoff run, depending how far it goes.
Bregman got off to a slow start with the Cubs this season but got rolling at the plate in the second half. He batted .241/.336/.359 over 45 games before the All-Star break and .296/.378/.600 through 44 games after the Midsummer Classic. Bregman has hit 17 home runs in the second half, nearly doubling his nine-homer total from the first half.
Besides National League MVP candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong, Bregman has been the Cubs' biggest offensive contributor in the second half. He would've been key to their playoff push and his absence will be rough for the lineup.
The National League Wild Card race is neck-and-neck as Bregman lands out of commission. The Cubs and San Diego Padres are currently tied for the first Wild Card spot with the Philadelphia Phillies trailing one game behind. Bregman won't be able to help his team fight for the best possible standing and they could end up facing a dangerous team in the first round, such as the Los Angeles Dodgers or Milwaukee Brewers.
Bregman also won't be able to stick it to the Red Sox, the team that traded its franchise third baseman to accommodate him, then didn't beat the best offer for his services in free agency. It's probably better for Boston that he doesn't have the chance to hit at Fenway Park again so soon.

Al already summarized what we know from the injury (and there likely won’t be another update until tomorrow due to today’s off day), but an uneasy question remains.
With six games remaining in the regular season and the Cubs one game from clinching a berth in the Wild Card round, today we need to take a closer look at what the Cubs offense and defense might look like if they are without their star third baseman for any length of time.
Even writing that sucks, a lot. After some early season struggles at the plate, Bregman is currently the second best hitter on the Cubs and it’s not particularly close. As I detailed less than a week ago, he’s been the second best hitter in all of baseball since the All Star Game, behind likely National League MVP, Pete Crow-Armstrong. Those numbers have shifted slightly since last week, with Fernando Tatis Jr. inching ahead of Bregman via fWAR in the last few games, but it’s still a potentially huge loss for any team.
It may be an even bigger loss for the 2026 Cubs than it would be for other teams in the Postseason hunt. The Cubs competitive edge is built almost entirely on elite offense and defense. You can see how the Cubs rank in a number of categories below:

The pitching has been questionable at the best moments and that success is built on the ability of the Cubs defenders to turn weak contact into outs while outscoring their opponents. The former is what allows them to win games where they are giving up way more runs than they should.
Bregman isn’t just a team leader. He isn’t merely the big free agent signing who has set the tone for the Cubs. He’s their second-best hitter since the All-Star break, and their third best hitter during the 2026 season (behind Seiya Suzuki). Alex Bregman has avoided the worst-case scenario after a scary incident on Sunday.
The Chicago Cubs star third baseman suffered multiple facial fractures after being struck by a foul ball while standing in the on-deck circle, but will not undergo surgery and is hopeful to return in the post-season, ESPN's Jeff Passan reported on Monday.
In the fourth inning, left-handed batting Michael Busch checked his swing and fouled off a pitch from Reds right-hander Luis Mey that struck Bregman, who immediately jogged toward the Cubs' dugout with his hand covering the left side of his face.
Bregman was escorted by a trainer down the dugout steps and into the clubhouse, with blood visible on his face. Matt Shaw replaced Bregman and drew a walk. He remained in the game to play second base, with Pedro Ramirez shifting to third.
“It just happens so fast,” Busch said. “(Mey)'s throwing the ball hard and it comes off hard. Any time it enters the head area, it's always a scary thing. We try to focus on the game, but it's tough. Hopefully he's OK, first and foremost.”
Bregman has contributed 26 home runs to a Cubs offence that leads MLB with 217 round-trippers. The 32-year-old also has .262/.352/.452 slash line and 89 RBIs.
The Cubs can clinch a playoff spot with either a win or an Arizona Diamondbacks loss on Tuesday.
—With files from The Associated Press

We’ve made it to the final week of the regular season. There are still two divisions in the American League up for grabs, a couple of long-shot playoff hopefuls looking to make a last-minute run, and playoff seeding to fight over. It should make for a dramatic end to a great season.
Our power rankings use a modified Elo rating system. If you’re familiar with chess rankings, you’ll know that Elo is an elegant ranking format that measures teams’ relative strength and is very reactive to recent performance. To avoid overweighting recent results during the season, we weigh each team’s raw Elo rank using our coin flip playoff odds (specifically, we regress the playoff odds by 50% and weigh those against the raw Elo ranking, increasing in weight as the season progresses to a maximum of 25%). The weighted Elo ranks are then displayed as “Power Score” in the tables below. As the best and worst teams sort themselves out between now and October, they’ll filter to the top and bottom of the rankings, while the exercise remains reactive to hot streaks and cold snaps. If you’re looking for a visual representation of the ups and downs of your team throughout the season, look no further than the brand new Power Rankings Board in the FanGraphs Lab.
First up are the full rankings, presented in a sortable table. Below that, I’ve grouped the teams into tiers with comments on a handful of clubs. You’ll notice that the official ordinal rankings don’t always match the tiers — there are times where I take editorial liberties when grouping teams together — but generally, the ordering is consistent. One thing to note: The playoff odds listed in the tables below are our standard Depth Charts odds, not the coin flip odds that are used in the ranking formula.

item.content:encoded:
A scary scene took place on Sunday when Chicago Cubs star Alex Bregman was hit in the face by a foul ball and force to exit the game against the Cincinnati Reds. After the game, Bregman posted a photo on his Instagram, telling fans that he will be fine, but also showing the damage the foul ball did.
Bregman may ultimately end up being just fine in the next week, but there is at least a chance he could land on the injured list and miss the rest of the regular season while the Cubs try to zero in on clinching a playoff spot.
How Bregman's injury impacts Cubs, playoff race
The Cubs would have the top wild card spot if the regular season ended today. They begin a three-game series on Tuesday night against the Miami Marlins, while the San Diego Padres face the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Philadelphia Phillies face the Milwaukee Brewers.
By strength of schedule, the Cubs have the easiest week of the three teams in wild card spots. But without Bregman, things could get a little bit more difficult. They'll face Bregman's former team, the Boston Red Sox over the weekend.
This could potentially hurt their chances of securing the top wild card spot and knock them down a bit in the standings, creating room for Philadelphia and San Diego to climb to the top. And if the Cubs are without Bregman at all in the postseason, then they will have tougher time getting out of the wild card round, as they could find themselves playing one of the other two wild card teams, or possibly even the Atlanta Braves.
The Cubs lost the NLDS last year to the Milwaukee Brewers, and they'll hope to make a deeper run this October, but any time without Bregman will make that task all the more difficult.
Bregman could be back in time for the postseason, so that could give the Cubs a better chance, but the timing of the injury certainly isn't good, especially with Chicago still trying to secure their wild card berth now that Milwaukee has already won the National League Central. It's going to be difficult to stay hot if he ends up landing on the injured list.
It will be interesting to see how he recovers and if he will be able to recover in time to help the Cubs in the playoffs.

Alex Bregman vivió un momento de preocupación durante la victoria de los Chicago Cubs por 9-1 sobre los Cincinnati Reds, luego de recibir un pelotazo en el rostro mientras se encontraba en el círculo de espera del Great American Ball Park.
El incidente ocurrió en la parte alta de la cuarta entrada, con dos outs. Michael Busch, compañero de Bregman, conectó una pelota de foul que terminó golpeando al tercera base en el pómulo izquierdo, debajo del ojo.
Bregman se dirigió inmediatamente al dugout y ya no regresó al encuentro. Matt Shaw entró en su lugar, mientras el cuerpo médico de los Cubs atendía al jugador.
La escena generó preocupación entre sus compañeros debido a que el pelotazo impactó directamente en el rostro.

El jugador fue trasladado a un hospital
Después de abandonar el terreno de juego, Bregman fue llevado a un hospital local para someterse a radiografías y una tomografía computarizada, con el objetivo de conocer el alcance de la lesión.
El manager de los Cubs, Craig Counsell, explicó que el pelotero tenía una cortada debajo del ojo, sangrado nasal y una inflamación considerable en la zona donde recibió el impacto.
“Tenía una cortada debajo del ojo. Le sangraba un poco la nariz. Está bastante hinchado”, explicó Counsell tras el encuentro. El manager también señaló que inicialmente pensó que el pelotero podía haberse fracturado la nariz, aunque todavía esperaban los resultados de los estudios médicos.

“Gracias por todos sus mensajes. Estaré de regreso”, escribió Bregman en Instagram.

Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman has returned to Chicago a day after being hit in the face by a foul ball while standing in front of the on-deck circle during a road game against the Cincinnati Reds.
Bregman shared that information — as well as a photo that appears to show that his left eye remains swollen shut — Monday morning on his Instagram Stories.
"Back in Chicago," wrote Bregman, who also appeared to have a cut and bruising near his left cheekbone where the ball off teammate Michael Busch's bat made contact during the fourth inning of the Cubs' 9-1 victory.
Read more: Is it still a rivalry? Dodgers complete sweep of woeful Giants
It was the second photo and update posted by Bregman since the gruesome injury occurred. On Sunday evening, the three-time All Star shared a photo that appeared to have been taken in the team's clubhouse. In addition to his eye being swollen shut and cheek cut, Bregman also has gauze inserted in his left nostril, where some bleeding had occurred.
"Thanks for the messages yall," Bregman wrote. "I'll be back."
Before the incident occurred, Bregman hit a run-scoring single in the first inning and walked and eventually scored in the third. He was standing several feet in front of the on-deck circle when Busch fouled off a pitch by Cincinnati's Luis Mey on a checked swing.
Read more: Dodger Stadium has a botanic garden tour. Meet the man entrusted with making it a draw
Bregman lost his bat but maintained his footing as the ball struck him. He covered his face with his left hand and was able to jog toward the Cubs dugout, where a trainer helped him down the steps and into the clubhouse. The 11-year veteran was taken to a hospital for testing.
"It's a terrible, terrible accident," Cubs manager Craig Counsell said after the game. "We hope he's OK."
Bregman is batting .262 with 26 home runs and 89 RBIs in his first season with the Cubs. He is probably best known to Los Angeles fans as a member of the Houston Astros team that defeated the Dodgers in the 2017 World Series and were later found by MLB to have illegally used technology to steal signs during that season. Bregman and the Astros also won the 2022 World Series.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

CINCINNATI -- The Chicago Cubs were somber after they defeated the Cincinnati Reds, 9-1, at Great American Ball Park on Sunday because Chicago was thinking about third baseman Alex Bregman, who was hit in the face by a foul ball off the bat of teammate Michael Busch.
Bregman was injured in the fourth inning with two outs. With the count, 1-2, Busch checked his swing at a pitch thrown by Reds right-hander Luis Mey. The ball made contact with Busch's bat, however, and then hit Bregman while he was in the on-deck circle. Bregman then ran towards the end of the Cubs' dugout before finally going into the clubhouse to get looked at by the team’s trainer.
Bregman was taken to a nearby hospital for X-rays and a CT scan, but the Cubs have yet to announce the seriousness of Bregman’s injury.
“I don’t know anything more than that,” Cubs manager Craig Counsell told reporters. “He had a cut under his eye. He was bleeding from his nose a little bit. It’s pretty swollen. It was below the eye. I honestly thought it hit him in the nose. I thought he had a broken nose, but I knew it hit him somewhere in the face. It’s just an unfortunate accident. I’m hoping and praying he is all right.
“We have to get good results from the hospital first. [Bregman] got hit in the face, so you are worried about his general well-being first. If we get a good report, we’ll move to the next step. I want to get a good report.”
Bregman is in his first season with the Cubs after signing a five-year, $175 million contract last January. He is having a productive season with the Cubbies, slashing .262/.352/.452 with 26 home runs and 89 RBI.
Before Sunday’s game, Bregman spoke to Yardbarker about his first season with the Cubs.
"The first half didn’t start out how I wanted it. (I) kept fighting. (I) trusted the process,” Bregman said. “I felt like myself over the last two months. That’s what I expect from myself. I’ve also been super thrilled to be in a position to continue to play postseason baseball, play meaningful games in October. I’ve been fortunate to do that every year of my career, which I don’t take lightly. I’m happy that we put ourselves in the position, so far, to be in.”
Bregman even had a word to say about teammate Pete Crow-Armstrong. To Bregman, PCA is the National League Most Valuable Player, and he has the stats to back it up.
Entering Tuesday’s action against the Marlins, Crow-Armstrong is leading the Majors with 10.5 wins above replacement (per FanGraphs) and 118 runs scored. He could also become the seventh player in MLB history to reach the 40-40 plateau.
“He has been the best player in the sport. It’s not even close,” Bregman said about PCA.

item.content:encoded:
The playoffs technically don't start for another week or so, but good luck telling that to teams for which every game already feels like October. With the standings in both the NL and AL as jumbled as they've been in recent memory, the stakes are already as high as can be — and whoever gets hot now could well ride that wave all the way to a World Series.
"Hot" could definitely describe both the San Diego Padres and Cleveland Guardians of late. The former has decided to just never lose again, not only grabbing hold of a Wild Card spot but now pushing for home-field in the first round if things break right. The latter, meanwhile, has once again snatched the AL Central while no one was looking. And they're not the only ones making serious moves in our latest MLB power rankings.
But who are we buying as serious title contenders, and who still has work to do? Read on to find out.
30. Colorado Rockies
The Rockies have admittedly let go of the rope of late, well on their way to yet another 100-loss season. There are at least some promising young hitters in this organization, which represents something to build upon moving forward. Of course, the pitching staff remains a mess, and no one's been able to crack that nut yet in Colorado.
–Chris Landers, FanSided.com editor
29. Los Angeles Angels
In Reid Detmers, Walbert Urena and Ryan Johnson, the Angels have at least some sort of foundation upon which to build for the future. Well, OK, maybe not Detmers, who will almost certainly be dealt this offseason. But still, L.A.’s pitching staff has been a real bright spot of late. The offense … well, that’s another question. Things are going to get worse before they get better under John Mozeliak. At least Arte Moreno is no longer around to meddle in it.
–CL
28. Athletics
The A’s are playing out the string of a lost season, although the contributions they’ve gotten from young bats like Henry Bolte, Max Muncy (not that one), Lawrence Butler and Zack Gelof down the stretch have been notable. None of that will matter, though, until the team fixes its pitching staff. We know we sound like a broken record, but it really is that simple, and no potential answers have emerged in the second half.
–CL
27. San Francisco Giants
Rafael Devers' injury, which figures to cost him at least some of next season as well as the end of this one, is a fitting if unfortunate end to what's been a miserable season by the Bay. Devers had been one of the few bright spots on this Giants team down the stretch alongside Bryce Eldridge; now, it's unclear how San Francisco will rebuilt its offense for 2027 in addition to finding reinforcements for a pitching staff that simply hasn't been good enough.
–CL
26. Kansas City Royals
The Kansas City Royals have been eliminated for quite some time now. If there is one clear goal for Kansas City this winter, it's to build a roster around Bobby Witt Jr. that is capable of making a postseason run. That is every team's goal, but the Royals are so far away from contention despite featuring such a prolific player, Witt Jr.'s career is closer to becoming Mike Trout's than Derek Jeter's.
-Mark Powell, FanSided.com MLB director
25. Minnesota Twins
At one point not all that long ago, the Twins had a realistic chance to make the playoffs as the third AL Wild Card spot. Then, the bottom fell out. Byron Buxton underwent successful hip surgery just last week that will keep him out until spring training, whenever that may be. The Twins once again experienced the roster flaw of building around an injured star.
-MP
24. New York Mets
This week couldn’t have been more awkward for the New York Mets when Pete Alonso hit his 300th home run in his return to Citi Field, much to the delight of many Mets fans in attendance, but once Alonso left town, the Mets began to play better, winning two games in a row against the Phillies. Those wins, headlined by more quality play from youngsters like Carson Benge, Zac Thornton and Christian Scott, show why Mets fans should be somewhat enthusiastic for what’s to come.
–Zach Rotman, FanSided.com staff writer
23. Cincinnati Reds
In the American League, the Reds likely wouldn't be the worst team in their division. But the NL Central has been a gauntlet all year long, and the Reds couldn't keep up. Despite breakthrough seasons from Elly De La Cruz and Sal Stewart, Cincinnati still has a long way to go on the starting pitching front. Can they rely on Hunter Greene and Chase Burns moving forward?
-MP
22. Seattle Mariners
Going 3-3 against the Angels and Rockies this week just about sums up this season in Seattle. The good news is that youngsters like Michael Arroyo and Lazaro Montes have helped to key an offensive turnaround. The bad news is that the starting rotation hasn’t held up its end of the bargain of late, and there are still tons of long-term questions about this lineup — especially with Randy Arozarena set to hit free agency. Jerry DiPoto will need to find some answers this offseason after a year in which just about everything went wrong.
–CL
21. Washington Nationals
The Washington Nationals deserved a better fate in 2026. Even with their offense falling off a bit of late, they’re still third in the majors in runs scored. The dynamic duo of CJ Abrams and James Wood is as good as any in the National League. Recently extended Cade Cavalli is a budding ace. Andrew Alvarez has thrown the ball incredibly well and looks like a future rotation stalwart. If it weren’t for a historically bad bullpen, we’d be talking about this team in Wild Card contention.
–ZR
20. Detroit Tigers
The Tigers have the best run differential in the AL Central and a pythagorean record of an AL playoff team. None of it matters. Scott Harris and the Tigers front office gave up on their team's postseason hopes at the trade deadline. Then, they proceeded to get fans' hopes up with a late August run, only to play like the team Harris assumed they'd become when it mattered most. The Tigers have some work to do, though the emergence of young stars in the lineup like Hao-Yu Lee and Kevin McGonigle, paired with Riley Greene's consistent play, give them some building blocks.
-MP
19. St. Louis Cardinals
The Cardinals are ahead of schedule, but not a postseason team. Make no mistake about it, St. Louis came crashing back down to earth in September, and has been eliminated from playoff contention. There are questions about the long-term future of Masyn Winn, especially with JJ Wetherholt as the de-facto shortstop of the future. But these are all good problems to have. Now, if only Bloom could find an ace burried in that farm system of his.
-MP
18. Baltimore Orioles
A series against league-best Milwaukee came at the worst possible time for the O’s, which now find themselves needing to hit an inside straight to snatch the final Wild Card spot. Pete Alonso’s heroics at Citi Field aside, Baltimore’s bats simply have not been good enough. Heck, no part of this team has; they’re hovering around .500 for a reason, after all, and there’s no reason to think they have the consistency required to get hot over the final week and overtake the White Sox, Blue Jays and Astros.
–CL
17. Miami Marlins
The Miami Marlins tried to do what they could to stick around in the NL postseason hunt, even using Sandy Alcantara on one day of rest in a save opportunity, but they were eliminated following Friday’s loss in San Diego. As disappointing as that is, the Marlins could finish above .500 for just the third time since 2009. That’s a sign that things are heading in the right direction for Miami.
–ZR
16. Toronto Blue Jays
The Jays have lost three of four series now, and news that Dylan Cease will have his next start bumped due to shoulder fatigue makes it even less likely that Toronto can sneak its way into the playoffs. With Trey Yesavage and Shane Bieber already on the IL, the rotation has begun leaking oil, and that’s not something this power-starved lineup is equipped to handle. The Jays still have a path to the final Wild Card spot, but it’s becoming an increasingly tenuous one, and it’s hard to see them making much noise even if they did get in.
–CL
15. Houston Astros
Getting swept at home by the Braves this weekend might well wind up costing the Astros a playoff spot. The closing schedule isn’t too tough, with trips to Seattle and Sacramento on tap. Still, if Houston doesn’t figure out where its high-powered offense went before it’s too late — and if Joe Espada can’t stop his bullpen from blowing late leads — Yordan Alvarez’s MVP season may well be for nought. As it stands, this looks like a team with fatal flaws that will spoil what could have been a deep run in a wide-open AL.
–CL
14. Chicago White Sox
Reality hit the White Sox real quick. Chicago has lingered around .500 for longer than they'd care to admit, and it was only a matter of time before the rest of the Central caught up to them. Munetaka Murakami has been dreadful since the trade deadline, and thus any contract extension talks have been put on hold. If the White Sox can hold on to a playoff spot, they'll be one of the best stories in October. If not, this season could all be for naught.
-MP
13. Texas Rangers
All of a sudden, the Rangers find themselves back in control of the AL West and home-field advantage in the first round of the playoffs. Of course, that says more about the West than it does about Texas; this is still a .500 team, one without a ton of depth on either side of the ball. The interesting thing, though, is that this lineup has finally started to show signs of life of late. Take care of business against the Twins and Mets this week, and no one’s going to want to face a team with Jacob deGrom and Nathan Eovaldi in the rotation plus an offense featuring Corey Seager, Wyatt Langford and Josh Jung.
-CL
12. Pittsburgh Pirates
The narrative Pirates fans are spinning these days is the same web every National League non-playoff team will get caught in this week; if only we played in the American League! Yes, the disparity between leagues is easy to blame for the Pirates shortcomings, but the front office also fell short in acquiring bullpen arms last winter, which could've kept Pittsburgh from blowing an extraordinary number of leads in the season's first half. That'll haunt these Pirates forever.
-MP
11. Arizona Diamondbacks
It's not Arizona's fault that their primary competition for a Wild Card spot, San Diego, has become one of the hottest teams in baseball over the last few weeks. Either way, though, Arizona has simply run out of bullets, especially in a rotation that hasn't gotten the boost from Corbin Burnes' return that they were hoping for. Eduardo Rodriguez has turned back into a pumpkin, and there's just not enough depth to keep pace with what's become a beast of an NL playoff chase.
–CL
10. Cleveland Guardians
Here we go again with the Guardians. Cleveland is a legitimate threat in a weak American League. Much like last season, the Guards are taking advantage of a fellow contender floundering down the stretch. This is when Cleveland plays its best baseball, so it should be no surprise they've won five straight games heading into Monday's potential postseason preview against the Red Sox.
-MP
9. Boston Red Sox
Dropping consecutive series to the Rangers and Rays won’t do much to Boston’s postseason outlook — they’ve been more or less locked into a Wild Card series in the Bronx for a while now — but it still doesn’t inspire confidence in this team’s ability to make a run come October. This offense is once again mired in a power outage, and while getting Willson Contreras and others back from the IL figures to help, who knows when that might actually be. And there’s still just a real dearth of power here that even this pitching staff might not be able to make up for.
–CL
8. Philadelphia Phillies
I don’t know what to think of the Philadelphia Phillies. On one hand, a rotation led by Zack Wheeler, Cristopher Sanchez, a healthy Jesus Luzardo, a rejuvenated Aaron Nola and a much-improved Andrew Painter should will them to wins. On the other hand, Luzardo is not healthy, the lineup is top-heavy and the bullpen, outside of Jhoan Duran, is an utter disaster. The Phillies are almost certainly going to make the playoffs, but their losses in New York this week ruined any last hope they had at a division title. And with how they’re playing right now, I don’t know if I’d pick them to get beyond the Wild Card Round.
–ZR
7. Chicago Cubs
The Cubs playoff parade was put on hold Sunday as Alex Bregman was struck in the face by a foul ball. Bregman was taken to the local hospital, and it's unclear how much time he will miss as of this writing. Chicago's postseason hopes may hang in the balance, as their one clear advantage over every other NL team is their lineup. The Cubs have scored the most runs in baseball this year.
-MP
6. San Diego Padres
Yes, the schedule has helped, particularly series against Miami, Colorado, Washington, San Francisco and Cincinnati. But no matter who they've played, the Padres look like a different team from the one we saw for much of the year, with their big bats finally mashing and their rotation coming into focus with Nick Pivetta now back in the fold. San Diego is now dead even with Chicago and Philly in the Wild Card race, and no one will want to face this lineup and this bullpen in a short series.
–CL
5. New York Yankees
Just when it seemed like New York was getting ready to make a move, with Aaron Judge finally back in the lineup after months on the shelf, the reigning AL MVP landed right back on the IL — this time with a calf strain that could well jeopardize his entire postseason. It’s been that sort of year for the Yankees, which have the pitching to keep believing in them as contenders but just haven’t been able to put it all together enough to take command of their own playoff destiny. And with a Judge-less offense and a penchant for mistake-filled baseball, winning three series in a row feels like a tough ask even in this AL.
–CL
4. Atlanta Braves
The Atlanta Braves punched their ticket to the playoffs this week, and thanks to the Phillies’ struggles, they’re on the cusp of winning the NL East — ensuring a top-three seed in the National League. Tyler Mahle pitched another gem, and Ronald Acuña Jr. is hitting his stride at the perfect time. There’re still some concerns with the team, like the No. 3 spot in their rotation and struggling stars like Austin Riley and Ozzie Albies, but getting to the playoffs is a big deal, and the Braves can take pride in checking that box.
–ZR
3. Tampa Bay Rays
The Rays may well have sewn up the AL East this week, taking two of three from the Red Sox over the weekend to stretch their lead over the Yankees ahead of an all-important four-game set in the Bronx beginning on Tuesday. Even if New York were to sweep all four, though, Tampa would still have the inside track to the division and the No. 1 overall seed. This pitching staff continues to thrive beyond all expectation even with some recent injuries, and the hitting has done just enough. Whether that recipe will withstand the postseason is the only question now.
–CL
2. Los Angeles Dodgers
Don't look now, but L.A.'s lineup has begun to stir, with Kyle Tucker looking like the player the Dodgers thought they were paying for this offseason. They also got Edwin Diaz back this week, and he's suddenly looking like the star closer of old — potentially answering this team's biggest question entering October. We know the rotation will be there; if they have Tucker at the height of his powers and a one-two punch in Diaz and Tanner Scott at the end of games, the three-peat march might be back on.
–CL
1. Milwaukee Brewers
The Brewers set a franchise record with 98 wins on Sunday. They still have a full week to go to add to that mark, and appear likely to reach the 100-win plateau. That's a great accomplishment, but it won't mean squat if Milwaukee falls to the Los Angeles Dodgers — or any other NL team for that matter — on their way to that elusive NL pennant. The Brewers are the favorites, but the Dodgers are lingering right behind them.
-MP

item.content:encoded:
Un momento completamente accidental encendió las alarmas en las Grandes Ligas. Alex Bregman, tercera base de los Chicago Cubs, terminó en el hospital después de recibir un fuerte pelotazo en el rostro durante el juego contra los Cincinnati Reds, pese a que ni siquiera se encontraba bateando cuando ocurrió el impacto.
¿Cómo ocurrió el accidente de Alex Bregman?
El incidente se produjo este domingo 20 de septiembre en el Great American Ball Park, cuando Michael Busch estaba en la caja ante los lanzamientos del dominicano Luis Mey. El pelotero de Chicago realizó un swing contenido y alcanzó a desviar la bola de foul, que tomó una trayectoria inesperada hacia donde Bregman esperaba su turno.
Con dos outs en la cuarta entrada, la pelota golpeó directamente a Bregman en el pómulo izquierdo, debajo del ojo. El antesalista reaccionó inmediatamente, soltó su bat y caminó hacia el dugout mientras se cubría la zona afectada con una mano.
La escena generó preocupación entre sus compañeros debido a la fuerza y ubicación del impacto. El manager de los Cubs, Craig Counsell, reveló posteriormente que el jugador presentaba una cortada debajo del ojo, inflamación y también sangrado por la nariz.
“Es un accidente terrible. Esperamos que esté bien”, señaló el estratega, quien admitió que inicialmente creyó que su pelotero podía tener la nariz fracturada debido a la violencia del golpe.
Chicago decidió retirarlo inmediatamente del encuentro. Matt Shaw entró como bateador emergente, mientras Pedro Ramírez posteriormente pasó a cubrir la tercera base. Los Cubs terminaron imponiéndose 9-1 sobre Cincinnati.
Alex Bregman fue trasladado al hospital
Debido a que la bola alcanzó una zona particularmente delicada, Bregman fue enviado a un hospital para someterse a radiografías y una tomografía computarizada (CT) con el objetivo de conocer la gravedad de la lesión y descartar daños mayores.
Michael Busch reconoció que continuar jugando después del episodio resultó complicado. El beisbolista explicó que todo sucedió en cuestión de segundos y manifestó su preocupación debido a que cualquier golpe en la cabeza genera alarma dentro del diamante.
Horas después, el propio Bregman dio señales alentadoras mediante sus redes sociales. El estadounidense publicó una fotografía donde apareció con el ojo izquierdo completamente inflamado, moretones y restos de sangre alrededor del rostro, una imagen que evidenció la fuerza del impacto.
Pese a lo aparatoso de su aspecto, acompañó la publicación con un breve mensaje para tranquilizar a sus seguidores: “Gracias por todos los mensajes. Volveré”.
El accidente llegó además durante una campaña importante para Bregman con los Cubs. El tercera base registra promedio de .262, 26 cuadrangulares y 89 carreras impulsadas en la temporada 2026, por lo que su evolución médica será seguida de cerca por Chicago en la recta final de la campaña.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox secured their spot in the postseason thanks to an Atlanta Braves win over the Houston Astros.
Things are going well now, but Red Sox fans remember the 10-17 start that led to Alex Cora and six other coaches being fired. Since then, interim manager Chad Tracy has led the charge in turning things around, but it has not all been him. The players started living up to expectations, and the team has gotten healthy.
At the time, many questioned Craig Breslow's ability to make decisions, with many fans saying Cora was fired as a result of Breslow failing to address the team's biggest flaws in the offseason. However, now it looks like Breslow was right to trust his players.
"I believed in the players that we had,” Breslow said when asked about the move to fire Cora, per The Athletic's Jen McCaffrey. “I felt it was really important that we acted definitively and decisively when we did so that we could create an environment around the players that was supportive, that would allow them to thrive. And they responded. While there may have been some people that questioned what this group was capable of, I think they answered resoundingly.”
One example of Breslow's belief paying off is Caleb Durbin. Durbin was acquired to replace Alex Bregman, and he was a terrible hitter through two months. However, after back-to-back off days in May, he has been on another level. He is looking more like the Rookie of the Year finalist he was for the Milwaukee Brewers last year. He looks like a real player the Red Sox can rely on down the line.
Perhaps what's most impressive about this Red Sox team is that they have turned the season around without arguably their two best pitchers, Garrett Crochet and Roman Anthony. However, Anthony is back, and Crochet could be in the bullpen for October.

Alex Bregman has made a smooth transition to life in the Windy City, tallying his highest bWAR total since his MVP-caliber campaigns with the Astros as a member of the Cubs this season.
His solid campaign screeched to a stunning halt on Sunday afternoon, however. Bregman was struck in the face by a foul ball from teammate Michael Busch during Chicago's win over the Reds.

Alex Bregman caught a ball to the face in the Chicago Cubs' latest game and the photo update looks terrible.
The Chicago Cubs have all but claimed their spot in the MLB playoffs following a 9-1 demolition of the Cincinnati Reds on Sunday.
The Cubs have fought hard all season long, and they are about to reap the rewards. For anyone doubting the first part of that statement, Alex Bregman's face is all the evidence needed.
The 32-year-old was simply minding his business on-deck during the fourth inning of their latest win when a foul ball caught him in the face. The results are not pretty.
Alex Bregman shared a picture of his swollen eye and injured face after the game
Bregman immediately went down clutching his face after he got hit, and he had to exit the game considering the severity of the impact.
He later posted a picture of his face on social media, and it is not for the faint of heart.
"Thanks for the messages, y'all. I'll be back," was all Bregman said, letting his face do most of the talking for him. That is a nasty bruise, and one that will likely take some time to heal.
As the regular season draws to a close, the Cubs will want to secure their postseason berth and then take some time to prepare for the business end of the season. They will be hoping a black eye that heals quickly is the worst thing Bregman has to deal with after this.

The Colorado Rockies are 57–99.
Purple Row After Dark: If the Rockies could steal one player
An absurd rule for absurd times: if the worst team in baseball could steal one player from a playoff club, who should the Rockies take?
One more loss will give them their fourth consecutive 100-loss season, and they are almost certainly going to finish with the worst record in baseball.
These are absurd times for the Rockies, so I have devised an appropriately absurd rule to help them out.
The team with the worst record in baseball gets to steal one player from a playoff team.
There are, naturally, some restrictions. We’re freezing the playoff field as it stood before games on Sunday, September 20. The player has to come from one of those 12 teams, cannot be a pending free agent, and you cannot take the player who leads his team in FanGraphs WAR. The Rockies also inherit the player’s existing contract.
No, one player is not suddenly turning the Rockies into a contender. But could one poached superstar at least keep this thing from becoming five consecutive 100-loss seasons?
Here’s the board:
| Team | Off limits: fWAR leader | Highest available fWAR | Other players worth considering |
| Rays | Junior Caminero (5.2) | Drew Rasmussen (4.7) | Jonathan Aranda (3) |
| Guardians | Parker Messick (4.6) | Steven Kwan (3.4) | Gavin Williams (3.4), Brayan Rocchio (3.3), José Ramírez (2.2) |
| Rangers | Ezequiel Duran (4.6) | Jacob deGrom (4.2) | Josh Jung (2.9), Wyatt Langford (2.8) |
| Yankees | Cam Schlittler (6.1) | Ben Rice (4) | Cody Bellinger (3.9), Aaron Judge (2) |
| Red Sox | Willson Contreras (4.1) | Payton Tolle (4) | Ceddanne Rafaela (3.9), Ranger Suárez (3.7) |
| White Sox | Miguel Vargas (5) | Chase Meidroth (4) | Tristan Peters (3.9), Sean Burke (3.1) |
| Brewers | Jacob Misiorowski (6.3) | Brice Turang (5.4) | Jackson Chourio (4), Jake Bauers (3.6) |
| Dodgers | Shohei Ohtani (6.7) | Yoshinobu Yamamoto (4.7) | Max Muncy (4.3), Andy Pages (3.9) |
| Braves | Chris Sale (5.7) | Michael Harris II (4) | Matt Olson (4), Drake Baldwin (3.1) |
| Cubs | Pete Crow-Armstrong (10.2) | Alex Bregman (5) | Dansby Swanson (3.6) |
| Padres | Fernando Tatis Jr. (5) | Jackson Merrill (4) | Ty France (3.8), Mason Miller (3.7) |
| Phillies | Cristopher Sánchez (5.8) | Jesús Luzardo (5.6) | Zack Wheeler (3.5), Bryce Harper (3.4) |
For me, the choice comes down to Brice Turang, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Aaron Judge.
Turang is probably the sensible choice.
At 5.4 fWAR, he would easily lead the Rockies, giving them a legitimate top-end player while immediately solving second base for the foreseeable future. He’s 26, hitting .266/.367/.441 with an .808 OPS, and brings value on both sides of the ball with elite range, strong baserunning and a 95th-percentile walk rate.
It would be a very easy way to make the roster better.
But the Rockies really need starting pitching.
Enter Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
He’s 14–8 with a 2.51 ERA, 178 strikeouts and a 0.87 WHIP over 179 innings. His Statcast profile is just as impressive: 100th-percentile pitching run value, 99th-percentile fastball run value, 95th-percentile offspeed run value and a 91st-percentile xERA.
Pitchers are risky, and Yamamoto comes with a lot of money attached. But it’s hard to argue with either the profile or the results, and the addition of the Penner family makes absorbing that contract a lot easier to imagine.
Speaking of high-priced items...
Aaron Judge.
Judge being available is basically a loophole created by our own stupid rule. Injuries have limited him to just 285 plate appearances, which is why he sits at only 2 fWAR, but he’s still hitting .241/.360/.511 with 15 home runs.
And the underlying numbers are still very much Judge: a .396 xwOBA, .569 xSLG, 94.0 mph average exit velocity and a 57.5% hard-hit rate.
It is very hard to look at that and say, “No thanks.”
After all, Aaron Judge is the type of hitter that, if he were playing 81 games a year at Coors Field, I might take out a small loan for season tickets.
So who are you stealing?

item.content:encoded:
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman shared a graphic selfie Sunday after suffering a frightening facial injury from a foul ball during an MLB game.
Bregman was struck during the fourth inning of Chicago's 9-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. Teammate Michael Busch fouled a pitch from Luis Mey, and the ball bounced into Bregman while he stood near the on-deck circle.
Bregman immediately left the game with blood visible on his face. He later underwent hospital testing after the ball struck him near his cheekbone.
The selfie, which he shared on his Instagram, showed significant swelling around Bregman's eye, along with facial cuts and a nosebleed. Especially the area below his eye had turned slightly black. He also included a message for supporters: "Thanks for all the messages, y'all. I'll be back 🙏."
Cubs manager Craig Counsell described the incident as a "terrible, terrible accident." He said the team's priority was getting positive medical results after Bregman was taken to the hospital.
The injury came during an important stretch for Chicago. The Cubs entered Sunday chasing a postseason berth and remained positioned for a National League wild-card spot.
Cubs must manage Alex Bregman's absence carefully

Bregman had already contributed during Sunday's game before leaving. He delivered an RBI single in the first inning, helping Chicago build an early lead.
After Bregman exited, Matt Shaw replaced him as a pinch-hitter. Pedro Ramirez shifted to third base while Shaw moved to second.
The Cubs continued producing offensively without their veteran third baseman. Pete Crow-Armstrong hit his 45th home run, while Michael Conforto and Seiya Suzuki also homered.
Chicago now faces a balance between its postseason push and Bregman's recovery. His defensive stability and veteran experience remain valuable during the final week.
Counsell said Bregman's general well-being came before baseball considerations. "I want to get a good report first," the manager said.
Bregman's message offered some optimism, but his return timeline remains unclear. The Cubs will need to await further medical updates before determining his availability.

CINCINNATI (AP) — Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman was taken to the hospital for tests after being struck in the face by a foul ball while standing in the grass several feet in front of the on-deck circle during Sunday’s game against the Cincinnati Reds.
There was no decision yet on whether Bregman, who was going for X-rays and CT scans, would travel with the team back to Chicago following its 9-1 win.
“He got hit in the left cheekbone essentially, under the eye,” Cubs manager Craig Counsell said. “I don’t know anything more than that right now. He was bleeding from his nose a little. There’s some swelling. It’s a terrible, terrible accident. We hope he’s OK.”
In the fourth inning, left-handed batting Michael Busch checked his swing and fouled off a pitch from Reds right-hander Luis Mey that struck Bregman, who immediately jogged toward the Cubs' dugout with his hand covering the left side of his face.
Bregman was escorted by a trainer down the dugout steps and into the clubhouse, with blood visible on his face. Matt Shaw replaced Bregman and drew a walk. He remained in the game to play second base, with Pedro Ramirez shifting to third.
“It just happens so fast,” Busch said. “(Mey)'s throwing the ball hard and it comes off hard. Any time it enters the head area, it's always a scary thing. We try to focus on the game, but it's tough. Hopefully he's OK, first and foremost.”
Bregman went 1 for 1 with a walk, an RBI and a run scored before leaving the game. He is batting .262 with 26 home runs and 89 RBIs after signing a $175 million, five-year free agent deal in January.
“I mean, at the end of the day, you just hope your friend is OK,” Pete Crow-Armstrong said. “That's the news that I'm hoping for. But scary stuff. Such a rarity.”
The Cubs could clinch a postseason berth with a Diamondbacks loss to the Yankees later Sunday.
Counsell said he hasn't thought about how a potential long-term absence for Bregman might impact his postseason roster plans.
“You know, we've got to get good results from the hospital,” Counsell said. “He got hit in the face (so) you're worried just about his general well-being first. I want to get a good report first.”

CINCINNATI (AP) — Pete Crow-Armstrong hit his 45th home run as the Chicago Cubs moved closer to clinching a postseason berth with a 9-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Sunday.
Chicago (87-69) reduced its magic number to one and could wrap up a berth if the Diamondbacks lose to the Yankees later Sunday.
The Cubs began the day tied with the Padres and one game ahead of the Phillies for the top NL wild-card spot which would earn them home-field advantage in the wild-card round. The Cubs own the tiebreakers over the Diamondbacks, Padres, and Phillies.
Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman left Sunday’s game in the fourth inning after being struck in the face by a foul ball off the bat of Michael Busch while standing near the on-deck circle.
Cubs left-hander David Peterson (9-8) allowed a run on three hits in seven innings with one walk and seven strikeouts.
The Cubs loaded the bases with one out in the third. Ian Happ singled in a run and Nico Hoerner walked to force in another to extend Chicago’s lead to 3-0. Pedro Ramirez’s two-run single made the score 5-0.
Reds right-hander Rhett Lowder (6-12) allowed five earned runs on six hits with three walks and three strikeouts.
Michael Conforto’s 15th home run made the score 6-1 in the fifth. Three batters later, Crow-Armstrong’s two-run home run made it 8-1.
Seiya Suzuki hit his 25th homer of the season in the eighth.
JJ Bleday hit his 23rd home run of the season for Cincinnati. Reds right-hander Carson Spiers allowed four runs and three homers in four innings. He also struck out five.
